As the grains traveled through the air, the wild winds of the Celestial Plains whispered, distorting their count—a trick of the shifting skies. Mora received the offering, planting the seeds in the fertile soil where they tripled in the warmth of the earth. The garden bloomed, heavy with the fruit of trust.

Now, Mora faced the sacred choice. She held the harvest, the measure of their eternal bond. To keep all was to break the cycle; to return a portion was to honor the genesis of the grain. She reached into the bounty, her hands guided by the memory of Aethel’s first offering. The wind howled again, obscuring the tribute as it returned to the Giver. Whether the return was fair or diminished by the gale, the cycle turned forever, anchored by the perilous, golden weight of faith. In this garden, trust is the only currency that grows, even when the truth is veiled by the mountain mists and the fickle, dancing spirits of the air.
